description.narrative: The development objective is to increase access to electricity in Ethiopia and to enhance institutional capacity for planning and implementation of the Government's electrification program.

The development objective of Electrification Program Project is to increase access to electricity in Ethiopia and to enhance institutional capacity for planning and implementation of the government's electrification program. The National Electrification Program (NEP) aims to achieve universal electrification by 2025. The NEP will be carried out in phases, with the immediate focus being on the early years of the Program (2018–2023). The NEP is organized into three pillars addressing the dominant challenges of the sector: (a) Pillar 1: Ongrid electrification; (b) Pillar 2: Off-grid service provisioning; and (c) Pillar 3: Sector capacity and institutional reform. Each of the pillars provides a specific menu of activities to be carried out to reach universal electrification. The phased focus under the NEP also allows for enhanced technical planning and coordinated fund mobilization. The PforR instrument is well suited to support the NEP. The PforR instrument allows the establishment of high-level, programmatic targets, compared with the traditional investment approach, with focus on project-based implementation. As such, the PforR instrument provides a unique opportunity to influence system wide improvements by supporting the GoE's flagship engagement in the electricity sector, that is, the NEP. The PforR allows the GoE to use and strengthen its own systems, which not only ensures longer-term sustainability of the NEP but also provides a unique window of dialogue on core issues.

title.narrative: Number of people provided with off-grid electricity services

comment.narrative: EEU has commissioned a total of 11 mini grids (five of those financed by ELEAP), supplying 3,946 household connections for a total of 19,730 people electrified. The 12th mini grid site in Gelehamur (Somali region), is under construction and the contractor has completed over 50 percent of the work. As part of the first restructuring in 2023, financing was reallocated in support of four additional commissioned mini grids (bringing the total of ELEAP financed mini grids to 9) in Behima, Benbaho, Tum, and Kusrewad. The recent verification by ESS found that the mini grids in Kusrewad and Behima are non-functional. In Kusrewad, high winds damaged the powerhouse, and in Behima, battery depletion rendered the system inoperable. During the mission in August 2025, EEU confirmed that the Behima mini grid is now operational after recharging using a DC battery. In Kusrewad, EEU revised the power house design and has mobilized a contractor to re-operationalize the mini grid.

title.narrative: Women in STEM: Percentage women's employment at EEU

comment.narrative: EEU has seen a slight increase in women's employment from 22.78% to 23%. Women's leadership sits at 13.34%. Other progress includes 12 women employees pursuing relevant further education that are fully funded under the scholarship program in the 2025-26 academic year. Jimma University has successfully carried out a women's capacity-building initiative for EEU, aimed at strengthening the skills and competencies. Given the positive feedback, the service contract with Jimma University is being extended. Employee feedback continues to be very positive about the EEU childcare services with 216 children being cared for across EEU offices, including the headquarters.

title.narrative: Improved planning and implementation capacity of the electricity sector

comment.narrative: A dedicated electrification team is set up in MoWE tasked with implementation and oversight of the national electrification agenda and ELEAP; MOWE has developed a capacity building plan to strengthen MOWE's mandate (the plan is under implementation); a Portfolio Management Office (PMO) is set up in EEU to strengthen managerial level oversight. A 5-year institutional plan for gender and citizen engagement in EEU is adopted and under implementation. Significant progress has been made in female employment, establishment of daycare facilities (across 13 regions), completion of customer satisfaction surveys, recruitment of in-house gender and CE experts, ongoing improvements to GRM, among others. EEU has also established an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) at the regional and national levels and will be expanding it to the district level.

Significant progress has been achieved with 1,604,161 verified grid connections established under the Program providing on-grid electricity services to over 8 million people.
